task: System-resource observability feature: new best-effort CPU/RAM/VRAM sampler module backing a planned GET /api/system/resources endpoint for the Activity page's system-resource strip (read-only; no scheduler/admission behavior change).

app/engines/system_resources.py.summary: New pure, synchronous, side-effect-free module (no import-time work, no threads, no persistent state, per modular_architecture.md). Exposes sample_resources() -> ResourceSample (TypedDict: cpu_pct, ram_used_gb, ram_total_gb, vram_used_gb: Optional[float], vram_total_gb: Optional[float]). CPU/RAM via psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None) (non-blocking) and psutil.virtual_memory(). VRAM via a best-effort `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits` subprocess call (2s timeout) that never raises — any failure (missing binary, timeout, non-zero exit, unparseable output) degrades to (None, None) for both vram fields, never a 500 upstream.

tests/api/test_system_resources.py.summary: Unit tests for sample_resources()/_sample_vram(), mocking only the true external boundaries (psutil.cpu_percent, psutil.virtual_memory, subprocess.run) per R2 — covers the normal case (all fields populated), nvidia-smi not found, timeout, and unparseable output (all degrade to vram=None without raising).

flow_impact: No existing callers yet — this module is not wired into a route in this commit. The GET /api/system/resources route wiring (app/api/routers/system.py) is a separate in-flight change; this entry covers the sampler module landing first. A follow-up queue entry will cover the route wiring once it lands, since that is the point this module gets a real caller and becomes reachable at runtime.
